name: FRELENA – AI Content & Social Media Automation
author: frelena

sections.description:
FRELENA connects your WordPress site to FRELENA (https://frelena.app), a software-as-a-service platform that writes articles, creates featured images, renders short vertical videos and publishes them to your social channels on a schedule.

The plugin is free to install. It contains the WordPress interface (business profile, articles, video, calendar, social and connection screens) and the code that saves the generated content into your site. The AI processing, video rendering and social publishing are performed by FRELENA Cloud, so a FRELENA account is required. A free plan is available; a paid monthly plan gives higher limits.

Languages: the interface follows the language of your WordPress user profile (or the site language). English and Bulgarian are included and further languages can be added through translate.wordpress.org. Generated content follows the language of your business profile / site.

Features

  • Business profile – describe your business once (services, audience, tone, preferred and forbidden words). A first draft can be prefilled from your own site content.
  • Articles – get suggested titles, generate full SEO-ready articles with a featured image, review them as drafts or let them be scheduled. Titles, key phrases and topics are checked against your existing posts to avoid duplicates. Yoast SEO fields are prefilled when Yoast is used.
  • Video – create short vertical videos (reels) from an article, from your own photos or from an uploaded video, with AI voice-over, music and subtitles.
  • Calendar – an editorial calendar that spreads articles, posts and videos evenly over time; reschedule or cancel any item.
  • Social – publish or schedule posts, stories, carousels and reels to connected Facebook Pages and Instagram professional accounts, and YouTube Shorts after your explicit approval.
  • Autopilot – an optional plan-driven schedule that keeps your site and channels active.

Getting started

  1. Register a free FRELENA account at https://frelena.app/ (or use your existing one).
  2. Connect the site in FRELENA → FRELENA Cloud.
  3. Fill in FRELENA → Business profile.
  4. Create your first article in FRELENA → Articles, then a video in FRELENA → Video.
  5. Optionally connect Facebook, Instagram and YouTube on the connection screen and plan posts in FRELENA → Calendar.

SaaS Service Disclosure

This plugin is an interface to the external FRELENA Cloud service operated by the plugin author. Without a connected FRELENA account the plugin does not generate, render or publish anything. All plugin code is included and fully available; plan limits (number of articles and videos per 30-day period) are enforced by the FRELENA Cloud service, not by locked code in the plugin.

Free and Paid Plans

  • Free – €0. Limited monthly number of articles and videos.
  • Optimal – €120 per month. Higher monthly limits.

Plans are purchased and managed on https://frelena.app/ – never inside WordPress. Current limits: https://frelena.app/. Usage periods are 30 days from the start of the subscription; a payment, renewal or plan change starts a new period.

Privacy and External Services

This plugin relies on external services. It only contacts them after you connect your site (FRELENA → FRELENA Cloud) and accept the data-sharing notice.

FRELENA Cloud – https://frelena.app (API: cloud.frelena.app)

Operated by the plugin author. Used for: account connection (email code), plan and quota status, article and image generation, video rendering, social publishing and scheduling.

What is sent and when:

  • When connecting: your email address, the site name and URL, WordPress and PHP versions, site language and the plugin version.
  • After connecting (once): a text snapshot of your home page, used to prefill empty business-profile fields.
  • When you use a feature: your business profile, the topics/keywords and instructions you enter, article text and images, photos or videos you upload for a video, and your social publishing choices.
  • When you click Upgrade or Increase the limit: the site asks FRELENA Cloud for a one-time checkout code for this site (no other data is sent), then your browser opens the payment page on https://frelena.app/ with that code. Payment is made on frelena.app, never inside WordPress.
  • When you send a recommendation (FRELENA → Recommend FRELENA): the email address you enter and your confirmation that you know the recipient. FRELENA Cloud sends that person one email with your name or company, your site address and your personal link, and stores the address only as a one-way hash with a masked form (for example jo***@example.com), so it is never emailed twice. The email contains a link to stop all further recommendation emails. The screen also loads your personal link, bonus and credit from FRELENA Cloud.
  • While connected: plan/quota status checks, only while an administrator uses the FRELENA screens or a FRELENA task runs; status of running jobs (articles, images, videos, social posts) is polled until they finish.
  • When an article cannot be finished: the task number and the technical reason (no personal data) are sent once to FRELENA Cloud, so the FRELENA team is notified and can fix the problem.
  • Optional, OFF by default (FRELENA → FRELENA Cloud → Privacy): every 15 minutes module health, WordPress/PHP versions and the site URL; PHP errors raised by FRELENA code with the request URL; the service may trigger a fixed list of built-in maintenance commands (health check, recovery of stuck jobs, rescheduling FRELENA cron events, refreshing the plan status, clearing FRELENA locks). Arbitrary code cannot be sent or executed.

The service stores the data needed to provide it (account, site, business profile, generated content and job history). Connection tokens for social networks are stored by FRELENA Cloud, not on your site. After disconnecting, the site no longer sends anything; data stored by the service is handled as described in the privacy policy.

To provide the service, FRELENA Cloud uses these providers on its own servers (your site does not contact them directly): OpenAI (text and image generation), Google Cloud Text-to-Speech (voice-over), YouTube Data API (YouTube publishing, only after you connect YouTube) and the Meta Graph API (Facebook/Instagram publishing, only after you connect them).

  • Terms of service: https://frelena.app/terms/
  • Privacy policy: https://frelena.app/privacy-policy/

Meta Graph API – https://graph.facebook.com

Only if you use the legacy direct Facebook publishing settings (page access token stored on your site): the plugin sends the post text, media URL and your page access token directly to Meta to publish the post. Meta terms: https://developers.facebook.com/terms/ – Meta privacy policy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/

YouTube

YouTube uploads are performed by FRELENA Cloud using YouTube API Services. YouTube Terms of Service: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms – Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

TikTok

TikTok posts are performed by FRELENA Cloud using the TikTok Content Posting API, only for videos you approve in the TikTok queue. TikTok Terms of Service: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/global/terms-of-service/en – TikTok Privacy Policy: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/global/privacy-policy/en
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress go to Plugins → Add New, search for “FRELENA” and click Install Now (or upload the ZIP via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin).
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to FRELENA → FRELENA Cloud, enter the email address of your FRELENA account, tick the consent box (data-sharing notice) and click to receive a code.
  4. Enter the 6-digit code from the email. The site is now connected to your FRELENA account.
  5. Fill in your business profile and start creating content.

Disconnecting

Go to FRELENA → FRELENA Cloud and click Reconnect. This deletes the connection key stored on your site and immediately stops all communication with FRELENA Cloud. Your posts, images and videos already saved in WordPress stay untouched. To disconnect a social network, open FRELENA → Connections and click Disconnect next to it. To delete your FRELENA account and the data stored by the service, contact FRELENA as described in the privacy policy.
sections.faq:
Is the plugin free?

Yes. The plugin is free and GPL licensed. Using the FRELENA Cloud service requires an account; a free plan is available and the paid plan is a monthly subscription.

Is an account required?

Yes. Text, image and video generation, rendering and social publishing are performed by FRELENA Cloud.

Does the plugin send data without my consent?

No. Nothing is sent until you connect your site and tick the consent box. Optional diagnostics/remote support is a separate setting that is OFF by default.

Does the plugin add a “Powered by” link to my site?

No. The plugin never adds a “Powered by” link, credit or any other FRELENA text to your site’s public pages, and there is no option to turn one on.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivation stops all FRELENA background tasks. Your posts, media, settings and scheduled items stay in WordPress, so reactivating continues where you left off. Deleting the plugin removes its code but keeps your posts and media; FRELENA settings stay in the database so that a reinstall keeps your connection.

Which social networks are supported?

Facebook Pages, Instagram professional accounts, TikTok and YouTube (Shorts, published only after your approval). Other networks are not supported in this version.

What do I need to connect my social networks?

  • Facebook: a Facebook Page on which you are an administrator.
  • Instagram: a professional account (Business or Creator) linked to that Facebook Page.
  • Meta business portfolio (optional): you can also connect through a Meta business portfolio that contains both the Facebook Page and the Instagram account. When connecting, select the portfolio and tick both.
  • TikTok: a TikTok account.
  • YouTube: a Google account with a YouTube channel.

Personal Facebook profiles and personal Instagram accounts cannot be connected, because Meta does not allow automatic publishing to them. A personal Instagram account can be switched to a professional one for free in the Instagram settings.

  • YouTube approval: the newest video is at the top of the list again.

3.2.196

  • Video from an article: every scene gets a new vertical image; the horizontal featured image of the article is no longer used in the video. A video can be made also for an article without a featured image.
  • Automatic video: when the monthly video quota is used up, the article shows “No videos left in the quota” instead of an error that is retried. Earlier articles with this error are marked once.
  • The “Upgrade quota” button (articles and videos) no longer gives “Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page” on a paid plan.

3.2.195

  • TikTok approval: the list of generated videos is removed. New videos go to the approval list automatically; older or skipped videos can be added with “Add for TikTok” in the video status table.

3.2.194

  • YouTube and TikTok approval lists: at most one video a day in each network. A proposed time that has passed, or a day that already has a video, moves to the next free day, also when new videos arrive.
  • Approving (also “Select all”) never schedules two videos on the same day in one network; a clear message asks for another day.
  • Videos whose storage period has expired, or that were deleted, are removed from the YouTube and TikTok approval lists.
  • The approval lists are sorted by publishing date, earliest first.

3.2.193

  • New users: “What FRELENA does for you” introduction and a “First steps” checklist on the Business profile screen. Each step changes colour by itself (not started, needs action, done, problem) based on what is already set up on the site.
  • Help button on every FRELENA screen with search and short written guides (where to start, articles, autopilot, own photos and videos, quotas, social networks, videos, troubleshooting).
  • Short tour of the FRELENA menu (WordPress pointers), started after the introduction or from “Show the tour”.
  • “?” hints next to the autopilot and own-media settings, and an empty state with “Quick create” on the Articles screen.
  • Works on phones; all new texts are translated to Bulgarian.

3.2.192

  • Video: above “Photos for the scenes” there is a tip with a ready-made prompt for making the 5 vertical scene photos yourself with an AI tool (format, position of the subject, no text), with optional style, atmosphere and theme at the end.
  • Video: “Copy prompt” button for the prompt.

3.2.191

  • Connections: the screen lists what is needed to connect each network (Facebook Page, professional Instagram linked to it or a Meta business portfolio with both, TikTok account, YouTube channel) and explains that personal Facebook and Instagram profiles cannot be connected.
  • Readme: new FAQ entry with the same requirements.

3.2.190

  • Articles: in the FAQ section, a question written as bold text becomes an H3 heading, the same as the other FAQ questions, for new and existing articles.
  • Articles: the “What you should know” box no longer gets the extra inner spacing some themes (e.g. Astra) add to every Group block; the spacing stays editable in the block editor.

3.2.189

  • Articles: older articles wrapped in article/section/aside elements are now also converted to editable blocks; the “What you should know” box becomes a Group block with the same aside tag. Links with non-Latin characters keep exactly the form they were written in.
  • Articles: a single timed-out article status check no longer sends an error report; the check repeats automatically and only repeated timeouts are reported as a warning.

3.2.188

  • Articles: on sites that use the block editor, articles are saved as regular blocks (paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, FAQ and the summary box), so every part can be edited directly instead of a Classic or Custom HTML block. Existing FRELENA articles are converted once in the background; their links, dates and statuses do not change. Sites with the Classic Editor or another editor keep plain HTML.

3.2.187

  • Articles: the focus keyphrase is no longer added in front of the first sentence (“keyphrase — …”) when the first paragraph already contains it; Yoast only needs it in the first paragraph. When it is missing, it is added with a capital first letter.

3.2.186

  • Articles: the floating status notice now covers every task in the table (“Being written: X · Waiting in the queue: Y”), so it no longer says the content is ready while other articles are still in progress.
  • Videos: the floating progress card you close stays closed for that video, also after a reload; it opens again only when the video is ready or fails.

3.2.185

  • Articles: a floating status notice you close stays closed – the automatic status refresh no longer brings it back. It shows again only when its text changes (a new status).

3.2.184

  • Articles: an article still waiting “In the queue” has a “Cancel” button. It has not started yet, so cancelling it uses nothing; the button disappears as soon as the article starts.

3.2.183

  • Articles: articles you start yourself (Quick create, With my guidance, My topics) ask FRELENA Cloud to write them on its faster tier, so they are ready much sooner. Autopilot and monthly content keep the economical tier.

3.2.182

  • Articles: the “Social networks” column showed “Queued” for articles that have no social posts at all (an empty stored value was counted as a post). It now shows “No social networks connected” when no network is connected, and the usual state otherwise.

3.2.181

  • Articles: safety net for “missed schedule”. If WordPress loses the scheduled event of a FRELENA article (it can happen when several posts are scheduled at the same moment), the article no longer stays “Scheduled” forever: the existing 15-minute FRELENA worker publishes FRELENA articles whose date passed more than 10 minutes ago, the same way WordPress would (duplicate protection included). At most 10 per run; no requests to FRELENA Cloud.

3.2.180

  • Articles: the focus keyphrase is the part of the title before the colon, taken whole up to 6 words. A longer part is shortened to at most 4 words that still make sense: never ending with a preposition, conjunction or particle, and cut before “и”/“или” when the rest does not fit. A keyphrase you enter yourself is not changed.
  • Articles: the address (slug) made from the keyphrase keeps only whole words that fit WordPress’s length limit, so it is no longer cut in the middle of a word (e.g. “…-и-електронн”).

3.2.179

  • Articles: when a task in “Content in progress” becomes ready again, its “Try again” and “Cancel and remove” buttons disappear right away, without reloading the page.

3.2.178

  • Articles: a focus keyphrase whose last word ends in л, р, М or Н (e.g. “Катастрофа с пострадал”) was cut in the middle of the last letter, so the finished article was rejected as “FRELENA Cloud returned an incomplete result”. The keyphrase is now taken correctly and the title stays exactly as suggested.

3.2.177

  • Articles: “Quick create” on a suggested topic that is already being generated also replaces it with a new suggestion, and topics being generated right now are no longer shown among the suggestions, so they cannot be started twice.

3.2.176

  • Articles: when an article cannot be created, FRELENA is notified automatically (the task number and the reason are sent to FRELENA Cloud), and the “Content in progress” table tells the site owner that FRELENA is checking.
  • Articles: after “Quick create” on a suggested topic, that topic is replaced by a new suggestion in the same place.
  • Deactivation also stops the social calendar worker and the health heartbeat, so WordPress no longer logs cron schedule errors after deactivation.

3.2.175

  • The built-in fallback quota for the Free plan (used only when FRELENA Cloud cannot be reached) now matches FRELENA Cloud: 3 articles.

3.2.174

  • Videos waiting in the FRELENA Cloud queue show “Waiting / Queued – place N”, and the time limit now counts from the start of processing, so a waiting video is not stopped.
  • A video task that FRELENA Cloud no longer has is marked as failed with a clear message instead of waiting forever.

3.2.173

  • “Content in progress” table: a removed task no longer comes back from the older single-task record, so rows of deleted articles really disappear.

3.2.172

3.2.171

  • Articles: the title and focus keyphrase are decided and checked before the article is written – against all articles, the generation history and the articles still being generated. A repeated title or keyphrase is never generated, and the article keeps the approved title.
  • The focus keyphrases of existing articles are also sent to the AI, so topic ideas avoid them.
  • A deleted article (also when moved to the trash) stops its running article, image and unfinished video tasks and leaves the “Content in progress” table. Scheduled videos and social posts stay.

3.2.170

3.2.169

3.2.168

3.2.167

3.2.165

short_description: Create AI-powered content, generate videos, schedule posts, and manage your WordPress content workflow through FRELENA Cloud.
description:
FRELENA connects your WordPress site to FRELENA (https://frelena.app), a software-as-a-service platform that writes articles, creates featured images, renders short vertical videos and publishes them to your social channels on a schedule.

The plugin is free to install. It contains the WordPress interface (business profile, articles, video, calendar, social and connection screens) and the code that saves the generated content into your site. The AI processing, video rendering and social publishing are performed by FRELENA Cloud, so a FRELENA account is required. A free plan is available; a paid monthly plan gives higher limits.

Languages: the interface follows the language of your WordPress user profile (or the site language). English and Bulgarian are included and further languages can be added through translate.wordpress.org. Generated content follows the language of your business profile / site.

Features

  • Business profile – describe your business once (services, audience, tone, preferred and forbidden words). A first draft can be prefilled from your own site content.
  • Articles – get suggested titles, generate full SEO-ready articles with a featured image, review them as drafts or let them be scheduled. Titles, key phrases and topics are checked against your existing posts to avoid duplicates. Yoast SEO fields are prefilled when Yoast is used.
  • Video – create short vertical videos (reels) from an article, from your own photos or from an uploaded video, with AI voice-over, music and subtitles.
  • Calendar – an editorial calendar that spreads articles, posts and videos evenly over time; reschedule or cancel any item.
  • Social – publish or schedule posts, stories, carousels and reels to connected Facebook Pages and Instagram professional accounts, and YouTube Shorts after your explicit approval.
  • Autopilot – an optional plan-driven schedule that keeps your site and channels active.

Getting started

  1. Register a free FRELENA account at https://frelena.app/ (or use your existing one).
  2. Connect the site in FRELENA → FRELENA Cloud.
  3. Fill in FRELENA → Business profile.
  4. Create your first article in FRELENA → Articles, then a video in FRELENA → Video.
  5. Optionally connect Facebook, Instagram and YouTube on the connection screen and plan posts in FRELENA → Calendar.

SaaS Service Disclosure

This plugin is an interface to the external FRELENA Cloud service operated by the plugin author. Without a connected FRELENA account the plugin does not generate, render or publish anything. All plugin code is included and fully available; plan limits (number of articles and videos per 30-day period) are enforced by the FRELENA Cloud service, not by locked code in the plugin.

Free and Paid Plans

  • Free – €0. Limited monthly number of articles and videos.
  • Optimal – €120 per month. Higher monthly limits.

Plans are purchased and managed on https://frelena.app/ – never inside WordPress. Current limits: https://frelena.app/. Usage periods are 30 days from the start of the subscription; a payment, renewal or plan change starts a new period.

Privacy and External Services

This plugin relies on external services. It only contacts them after you connect your site (FRELENA → FRELENA Cloud) and accept the data-sharing notice.

FRELENA Cloud – https://frelena.app (API: cloud.frelena.app)

Operated by the plugin author. Used for: account connection (email code), plan and quota status, article and image generation, video rendering, social publishing and scheduling.

What is sent and when:

  • When connecting: your email address, the site name and URL, WordPress and PHP versions, site language and the plugin version.
  • After connecting (once): a text snapshot of your home page, used to prefill empty business-profile fields.
  • When you use a feature: your business profile, the topics/keywords and instructions you enter, article text and images, photos or videos you upload for a video, and your social publishing choices.
  • When you click Upgrade or Increase the limit: the site asks FRELENA Cloud for a one-time checkout code for this site (no other data is sent), then your browser opens the payment page on https://frelena.app/ with that code. Payment is made on frelena.app, never inside WordPress.
  • When you send a recommendation (FRELENA → Recommend FRELENA): the email address you enter and your confirmation that you know the recipient. FRELENA Cloud sends that person one email with your name or company, your site address and your personal link, and stores the address only as a one-way hash with a masked form (for example jo***@example.com), so it is never emailed twice. The email contains a link to stop all further recommendation emails. The screen also loads your personal link, bonus and credit from FRELENA Cloud.
  • While connected: plan/quota status checks, only while an administrator uses the FRELENA screens or a FRELENA task runs; status of running jobs (articles, images, videos, social posts) is polled until they finish.
  • When an article cannot be finished: the task number and the technical reason (no personal data) are sent once to FRELENA Cloud, so the FRELENA team is notified and can fix the problem.
  • Optional, OFF by default (FRELENA → FRELENA Cloud → Privacy): every 15 minutes module health, WordPress/PHP versions and the site URL; PHP errors raised by FRELENA code with the request URL; the service may trigger a fixed list of built-in maintenance commands (health check, recovery of stuck jobs, rescheduling FRELENA cron events, refreshing the plan status, clearing FRELENA locks). Arbitrary code cannot be sent or executed.

The service stores the data needed to provide it (account, site, business profile, generated content and job history). Connection tokens for social networks are stored by FRELENA Cloud, not on your site. After disconnecting, the site no longer sends anything; data stored by the service is handled as described in the privacy policy.

To provide the service, FRELENA Cloud uses these providers on its own servers (your site does not contact them directly): OpenAI (text and image generation), Google Cloud Text-to-Speech (voice-over), YouTube Data API (YouTube publishing, only after you connect YouTube) and the Meta Graph API (Facebook/Instagram publishing, only after you connect them).

  • Terms of service: https://frelena.app/terms/
  • Privacy policy: https://frelena.app/privacy-policy/

Meta Graph API – https://graph.facebook.com

Only if you use the legacy direct Facebook publishing settings (page access token stored on your site): the plugin sends the post text, media URL and your page access token directly to Meta to publish the post. Meta terms: https://developers.facebook.com/terms/ – Meta privacy policy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/

YouTube

YouTube uploads are performed by FRELENA Cloud using YouTube API Services. YouTube Terms of Service: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms – Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

TikTok

TikTok posts are performed by FRELENA Cloud using the TikTok Content Posting API, only for videos you approve in the TikTok queue. TikTok Terms of Service: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/global/terms-of-service/en – TikTok Privacy Policy: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/global/privacy-policy/en
